capabilities.description: The optional features this backend supports (flight-analyses, flight-events, arrival-search, iata-flight-types and, while their setting is enabled, divert and auto-update), the same names as the X-SmartCARS-Capability response header. get.description: Search for available flights with optional parameters to filter a search. Results are ordered by route distance (the great-circle distance between the two airports, shortest first; a flight whose airport has no coordinates comes last), then departure airport, then arrival airport, then flight id, so a route's flights are always adjacent. A page holds at most limit flights (250 at most). When more results follow, the X-SmartCARS-Next-Cursor header carries a cursor: repeat the same request with it as cursor to get the next page. The totals headers count every matching flight, across all pages. A client that ignores the headers gets the first page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of flights on the page

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The X-SmartCARS-Next-Cursor value of the previous page, to get the page after it. Opaque; it does not expire. Flights added or hidden between pages are neither skipped nor repeated among the remaining results. The other parameters are repeated unchanged.

parameters.name: departureAirport
parameters.description: The ICAO code for the departure airport

parameters.name: arrivalAirport
parameters.description: The ICAO code for the arrival airport

parameters.name: aircraft
parameters.description: The ID of an aircraft; only flights a subfleet containing it can fly are returned, none for an unknown ID. A non-numeric value is ignored

parameters.name: callsign
parameters.description: A callsign pattern to search for (does not have to be exact)

200.description: 200 - Return a page of the available flights

X-SmartCARS-Next-Cursor.description: Present when more results follow; send it back as cursor to get the next page. Absent on the last page.

X-SmartCARS-Total-Flights.description: The number of flights matching the search, across all pages.

X-SmartCARS-Total-Routes.description: The number of distinct departure and arrival airport pairs among the matching flights.

400.description: 400 - Invalid type, or a malformed cursor (message Invalid cursor)

post.description: Search for flights across three dimensions: any of several departure airports, optionally any of several arrival airports, and optionally any of several aircraft. Results are ordered by route distance (the great-circle distance between the two airports, shortest first; a flight whose airport has no coordinates comes last), then departure airport, then arrival airport, then flight id, so a route's flights are always adjacent. A page holds at most limit flights (250 at most). Without perArrivalLimit the search is paged: when more results follow, the X-SmartCARS-Next-Cursor header carries a cursor, sent back as cursor with the rest of the body unchanged to get the next page, and the totals headers count every matching flight across all pages. A client that ignores the headers gets the first page. When perArrivalLimit is given, at most that many flights are kept per arrival airport, in the same order, before the overall limit is applied; that answer is not paged, carries none of the three headers and ignores cursor. When the only-flights-from-current-airport setting is on, the pilot's current airport is used as the only departure, whatever the request says.

departureAirports.description: The ICAO codes of the possible departure airports; unknown codes are ignored

arrivalAirports.description: The ICAO codes of the possible arrival airports; unknown codes are ignored. When omitted or empty, every arrival is searched

aircraft.description: The ids of the aircraft; only flights whose subfleets contain one of them are returned. When omitted or empty, no aircraft filter applies

limit.description: The maximum number of flights on the page

perArrivalLimit.description: The maximum number of flights to keep per arrival airport, taken in route distance order before limit is applied. Turns paging off

cursor.description: The X-SmartCARS-Next-Cursor value of the previous page, to get the page after it. Opaque; it does not expire. Flights added or hidden between pages are neither skipped nor repeated among the remaining results. Ignored when perArrivalLimit is given

200.description: 200 - Return a page of the available flights

X-SmartCARS-Next-Cursor.description: Present when more results follow; send it back as cursor to get the next page. Absent on the last page and when perArrivalLimit is given.

X-SmartCARS-Total-Flights.description: The number of flights matching the search, across all pages. Absent when perArrivalLimit is given.

X-SmartCARS-Total-Routes.description: The number of distinct departure and arrival airport pairs among the matching flights. Absent when perArrivalLimit is given.

400.description: 400 - Missing departureAirports, or a malformed cursor (message Invalid cursor)

post.description: Cancel an ongoing flight. The unfiled PIREP is cancelled. With the `smartcars.cancel_mode` setting at `delete` it is then deleted together with its ACARS positions, logs and flight analyses, and a SimBrief OFP stays attached to the booked flight; at `cancel` (the default) it stays as a cancelled PIREP. Only the calling pilot's own PIREP is touched; a PIREP that is unknown, already cancelled or deleted, or owned by another pilot answers 200 as well, so the call can be repeated safely. In `delete` mode, a PIREP left in the cancelled state by an earlier call that failed part way is deleted on the next call.

post.description: Record a diversion on an ongoing flight using phpVMS's own diversion handling. The airport is stored in the PIREP's "diversion-airport" field and the PIREP status becomes DV; phpVMS then moves the aircraft and pilot to that airport when the PIREP is filed. A second call replaces the airport. Sending the booked arrival airport removes the diversion again and leaves the status as is; the next /flights/update sets it from the flight phase. While a diversion is recorded, /flights/update keeps the DV status during takeoff, climb, enroute, approach and landing. Only available when the phpVMS "pireps.handle_diversion" setting is on.

uuid.description: The PIREP ID (a phpVMS hash ID) of the ongoing flight

airport.description: The phpVMS airport ID of the diversion airport, case-insensitive

200.description: 200 - The diversion was recorded (or cleared)

404.description: 404 - No such flight for this pilot

409.description: 409 - The flight is not in progress

422.description: 422 - Unknown airport, or diversion handling is disabled for this VA

post.description: Store flight log lines while the flight is in progress, before it is filed. Each line becomes a phpVMS ACARS log row (type LOG) of the PIREP, shown in the flight log on the PIREP page and in the admin, with the line's message (cut to 255 characters) and its timestamp as the row's time. The row ID is derived from the PIREP ID and the line's index, so the request is idempotent: a line sent again with an index already stored is ignored and the first stored text and time stay. At /flights/complete, a flightData item whose eventId matches an index already stored is not stored a second time; the other items are stored as before. A batch is checked as a whole: one invalid entry refuses the whole request and stores nothing. Expect a client to retry on any status other than those listed (a 500, for example): it sends the same lines again later.

uuid.description: The PIREP ID (a phpVMS hash ID) of the ongoing flight

bidID.description: The booking of the flight; accepted but not used

events.description: The log lines, at most 100 per request

index.description: The line's 0-based position in the flight log, the same number the line has as eventId in the flightData filed with /flights/complete

type.description: The kind of line; checked, not stored

message.description: The line's text, the flightData item's message; may be empty. phpVMS's request middleware trims it and turns an empty or blank one into null, stored as null (no log text); otherwise stored cut to 255 characters

timestamp.description: The line's UTC time, the flightData item's eventTimestamp (e.g. 2026-11-06 14:05:00z)

200.description: 200 - The lines were stored (lines already stored are left as they are)

404.description: 404 - No such flight for this pilot

409.description: 409 - The flight is not in progress (already filed or cancelled)

422.description: 422 - events is not an array, is empty or has more than 100 entries, or an entry lacks an integer index >= 0, a type of info, event or comment, a message (a string, empty allowed) or a parseable timestamp

post.description: Complete and file a PIREP for an ongoing flight. Only the calling pilot's own PIREP is filed. A PIREP that was already filed (pending, accepted or rejected) is left untouched and its ID is returned again, so the call can be repeated safely, including after a failure that happened once the PIREP was saved.

uuid.description: The PIREP ID (a phpVMS hash ID) of the ongoing flight

aircraft.description: Optional. The aircraft flown; when it differs from the PIREP's aircraft the PIREP takes it only if it exists, the pilot may fly its subfleet, it is parked and no other flight or pilot holds it (otherwise the PIREP keeps its aircraft). Fares are not regenerated

network.description: Optional. The network flown on, stored as the PIREP's Network field value

simVersion.description: Optional. The simulator and its version, stored as the PIREP's Simulator field value

score.description: Optional. Flight score out of 100, stored rounded as the PIREP's score

cruiseLevel.description: Optional. Cruise level in feet, stored rounded as the PIREP's flight level

blockFuel.description: Optional. Fuel on board at off-block in lbs; without it the block fuel is read from the pushback log line

zfw.description: Optional. Zero fuel weight in lbs

distanceFlown.description: Optional. Distance flown in nautical miles; without it the distance is computed from the positions

blockTime.description: Optional. Block time (off-block to on-block) in decimal hours. Accepted and not stored: phpVMS has no block time column, blockOffTime and blockOnTime carry it

blockOffTime.description: Optional. Off-block time, ISO 8601 UTC; without it the server time of the first airborne update stays. Ignored (the stored times kept) when it would fall after the on-block time, sent or stored

blockOnTime.description: Optional. On-block time, ISO 8601 UTC; without it the server time of the landed update stays (or the filing time). Ignored (the stored times kept) when it would fall before the off-block time, sent or stored

passengers.description: Optional. Passengers flown; replaces the PIREP's passenger fares, split over them in proportion to their capacity

cargo.description: Optional. Cargo flown in lbs (converted to kg when the VA's weight unit is kg); replaces the PIREP's cargo fares, split over them in proportion to their capacity

200.description: 200 - Flight was successfully finished, or had already been filed

pirepID.description: The ID of the filed PIREP

405.description: 405 - The POST method was not used

409.description: 409 - The flight is neither in progress nor filed (cancelled, deleted or a draft)

post.summary: GitHub push webhook for the module auto-update
post.description: Receives a GitHub push webhook signed with the auto-update secret (X-Hub-Signature-256, HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body). On a push to master of the fork it queues an update job, which downloads that commit from GitHub itself; the request never carries code. Does nothing while the auto-update setting is off. Not called by smartCARS.

parameters.description: sha256=<HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body with the webhook secret>

parameters.name: X-GitHub-Event
parameters.description: push (acted on), ping (answered), anything else ignored

schema.description: The GitHub push payload; ref, after, deleted and repository.full_name are read

200.description: Auto-update is disabled (nothing done), or a ping answered

202.description: Update queued, or the event or push ignored (another event, another ref, a deleted branch)

401.description: Missing or invalid signature, or no secret configured

post.description: Store the smartCARS analyses of a finished flight (landing, flight score, takeoff, trails and debrief), replacing any earlier upload for the same PIREP. Only the calling pilot's own PIREPs are accepted. The payloads are stored as JSON in the sc_flight_analyses table; each part is stored exactly as sent (taken from the raw request body, so empty strings and empty objects survive) and returned the same way by /pireps/analyses/search; the touchdown rate, landing grade and blended flight score are also copied into their own columns. Cancelling a flight deletes its row.
